messages:
anya: Quick flag — hit a case where requests were routed to fallback then immediately to quota fallback, producing two degrade breadcrumbs for the same user request. Feels noisy in audit logs and confusing in the console.

mike: Uh, yeah that rings a bell. We're firing routing-policy triggers on `5xx_rate > 1%` in 60s and quota-circuit fires on `token_burst > 80%`. They can coincide on spikes.

suresh: The core problem is we have two independent decisioners with separate telemetry windows. We should harmonize the precedence so the UI shows a single decision path.

jess: UX note — from a customer perspective we should surface one canonical reason + a collapsed history of follow-on actions. Showing two top-level failures looks like two separate incidents.

anya: Agreed. Proposal: canonicalize on a single fallback_reason field on the request envelope, e.g. `fallback_reason: routing_policy` with `secondary_reasons: [quota]`. That'd make audit playback less noisy.

mike: Implementation-wise we can add `fallback_reason` to the routing response and have the quota-controller respect it if it's within the same request lifetime (<= 5s). If quota fires later, append to `secondary_reasons`.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout for eng-platform/fallback-coordination started -> sha abc123 -> 3/10 hosts

lina: Telemetry ask: we need a single event type `fallback.decision` with fields: `primary_reason`, `secondary_reasons` (array), `decision_time_ms`, `trace_id`, `policy_snapshot_id`. Without those it's hard to correlate.

suresh: +1. Also include `policy_match_details` string blob so audit can replay the predicate (e.g., `5xx_rate=1.2% window=60s`). That keeps UI simple but lets engineers dig in.

jess: For Console UX, show the primary reason and a "see full evidence" link that opens the replay timeline. If secondary reasons exist, show them under an expandable section.

anya: Edge case: what if quota detects a sustained token exhaustion earlier but routing policy blocked a hot path later? Which is primary? I think the thing that triggered the first deny in the call path should be primary.

mike: Good call. We'll use chronological priority: earliest deny -> primary. Routing policy might be proactive (predictive), though, so we need a tiebreaker: explicit operator overrides. Add `operator_override` tag if user pressed an escape hatch.

lina: For audit retention, we should keep the entire `fallback.decision` event and associated policy snapshots for 90 days by default for enterprise customers. That aligns with support playbooks.

suresh: Quick config proto (WIP):
```yaml
fallback_coordination:
  precedence: chronological # options: chronological | policy_priority
  primary_timeout_s: 5
  telemetry_event: fallback.decision
```

jess: UX question: when we collapse multiple reasons, do we still increment metrics per-reason? Support wants per-reason counts for billing/alerts.

anya: We should increment both: primary increments `fallback.primary.<reason>`, and secondary increments `fallback.secondary.<reason>`. That way signals survive the collapse.

mike: I'll wire the event schema and ensure the decisioner code writes `fallback_reason` into the response envelope. Suresh can help merge quota-controller to respect it.

suresh: Happy to. I'll open a PR that adds the `secondary_reasons` field and a short unit test for the 5s request lifetime coercion.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary update -> hosts healthy 3/3, canary complete

jess: I'll mock the console view with collapsed breadcrumbs so we can validate with design review tomorrow.

anya: Thanks all — follow-ups: mike (schema PR), suresh (quota merge), jess (console mock), lina (telemetry retention policy). I'll create a ticket and link PRs.

mike: Filed https://redwoodinternal/issue/INFR-2019 with checklist.

suresh: PR: https://redwoodinternal/pr/4821 - WIP, tests added.

jess: Design proto in Figma: https://figma.com/file/xyz - will add notes for audit playback UX.

anya: Closing loop — aim to ship in next sprint unless objections. :thumbsup:

lina: :thumbsup: lets also add an alert if both reasons fire within 1s — that's a good signal of system-level instability.

mike: noted, will add `coincident_fallback_alert` boolean in telemetry.

anya: Great. End thread.
